subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification — FinPay follow-up
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finpay.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + pricing info request (Dedicated)

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a few asks to help us size Dedicated correctly and surface a preliminary commercial range: 

Summary:
- Use case: FinPay anomaly detection + conversational support for merchants (inference-heavy, moderate to high concurrency).
- Current monthly token volume: ~50M (primarily scoring and short chats).
- Growth expectation: target up to ~200M tokens/month within 12 months if model Latency and unit economics are within budget.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for 256-512 token responses; occasional longer tails OK for batch jobs.

Asks (helps us size Dedicated pool and GPU type):
1) Token volume profile: monthly average and peak monthly or weekly volumes (if you have that split).
2) Target budget range for committed reserved capacity (monthly).
3) Target unit economics (ballpark $/1M tokens). If you have a target $/1M tokens we should aim for with Dedicated, please share.
4) Preferred GPU type or requirement: A100-80GB, H100-80GB, or open to our recommendation.
5) Throughput targets: target sustained tokens/sec and peak concurrency (requests per second for typical 512-token responses).

Next steps I propose:
- Share rough numbers (answers above) — I can return a sizing + price band.
- If numbers look aligned, schedule a 30–45m technical sizing with Aditya (solutions) to confirm latency/throughput and Marissa for commercial.

I attached our Dedicated pricing one-pager for reference. I looped Aditya and Marissa so we can move quickly once you share numbers.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dedicated-pricing.pdf
From: Samir Shah <samir@finpay.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + pricing info request (Dedicated)

Hi Camila —

Thanks for the clear recap. Answers below so you can start sizing: 

1) Token volumes:
- Current: ~50 million tokens/month across scoring + chat (mostly scoring).
- Expected (12 months): ~200 million tokens/month assuming successful pilot and merchant uptake.
- Peak: during end-of-month batch scoring we see spikes ~1.5–2x baseline for ~4–6 hours.

2) Budget range:
- We’re targeting committed spend in the range of $10k–$20k/month for reserved capacity to start. Could expand if unit economics justify it.

3) Target unit economics:
- Ideally want to see $/1M tokens in the ballpark of $25–$40 for inference (including basic batching/caching). Anything above ~$50/1M will be hard to pencil right now.

4) GPU preference:
- Prefer H100 if it materially improves latency/cost for our models. Open to recommendations from your sizing team.

5) Throughput/latency:
- Typical request size: prompt ~50 tokens, response ~256 tokens (average).
- Target sustained throughput: ~200 tokens/sec across our active pool (for 512 token end-to-end).
- Peak concurrency: expect up to ~20 concurrent requests at peak business hours.

Procurement contact for contracting: procurement@finpay.com

Happy to take the tech sizing next week — share a few slots and we’ll pick one.

Best,
Samir Shah
Director of AI Products
FinPay
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finpay.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + pricing info request (Dedicated)

Appreciate the quick details, Samir — this is perfect. A few notes and a proposed next step.

Sizing notes (ballpark, subject to Aditya validation):
- Given your growth to ~200M tokens/mo and the throughput/latency targets, a starting Dedicated pool using H100s looks like the right fit.
- Initial reserved capacity we’d likely propose: H100 x8 (reserve) with autoscale/burst options. That configuration should give you headroom for 200M tokens/mo with room for batching and KV caching to reduce per-token cost.
- Expected baseline throughput (512 token request profile): ~180–260 tokens/sec sustained depending on batching, plus higher short-term burst capacity.
- Preliminary unit cost estimate (with expected batching/caching and workload assumptions): around $25–$35 per 1M tokens. This aligns with your target range; exact number depends on request distribution and effective batching.

Immediate next steps:
1) Technical sizing call (30–45m) with Aditya to validate model family, sequence length distribution, and test a 1–2 hour load profile if needed. Please suggest a few slots next week.
2) Marissa will prepare a draft commercial band and outline reserved vs burst pricing and minimum commit options.

Can you also confirm the model family you plan to serve (open models like Llama-variant, or a commercial model) and whether you need encryption/KMS integration for Private deployments? That impacts GPU selection and licensing.

I attached a quick usage CSV to show the kind of breakdown Aditya might ask for.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning schedules.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com

Camila —

Thanks — confirming a few items and proposing times.

Model details: we plan to serve an open Llama2-derived 70B variant (quantized weights), with average prompt/response sizes as I shared (50/256). No enterprise-licensed commercial model for now. We will need KMS integration for keys (we’ll share the KMS contact during procurement).

Procurement: procurement@finpay.com is the right contact for statements of work and PO flow.

Available slots for a 30–45m technical + pricing call next week (Pacific):
- Tue 17 Feb 2026 10:00–11:00 PT
- Wed 18 Feb 2026 14:00–15:00 PT
- Thu 19 Feb 2026 09:00–10:00 PT

We prefer H100 if your sizing validates a clear benefit. If you can send a preliminary H100 x8 estimate and what a smaller H100 x4 baseline would look like (cost + expected throughput), that would help our internal eval.

Thanks,
Samir
